articles.summary: Iceland voted against resuming talks to join the European Union, officials announced Sunday, as concerns over sovereignty trumped arguments for European integration. Icelandic voters rejected the measure amid widespread concern over maintaining control over fishing rights , a backbone of the country’s economy. The vote, which showed domestic concerns overriding geopolitical ones, comes as the resource-rich Arctic gains strategic importance , with US President Donald Trump pushing to acquire neighboring Greenland. Supporters of EU membership argued that closer ties with Europe could help strengthen the country’s security. The vote’s result is “a clear setback for Brussels,” an EU diplomat told Reuters, as the bloc seeks greater strategic weight at a time when European “security challenges are acute ,” a Carnegie Endowment scholar wrote. — Lauren Morganbesser

articles.summary: In summary California prosecutors would gain new powers to sue big businesses over alleged anti-competitive practices under a bill Democratic lawmakers sent to Gov. Gavin Newsom. A California lawmaker scaled down her bill to let the “little guy” sue big business, and the compromise helped her anti-monopoly proposal reach Gov. Gavin Newsom’s desk. Assembly Bill 1776 , nicknamed the Compete Act, was the subject of hot debate throughout the legislative session, pitting powerful consumer groups and unions against the state’s Chamber of Commerce and biomedical companies, including drugmakers. If approved by the governor, it would allow the attorney general of California and district attorneys to sue individual businesses for using what bill backers view as unfair tactics to strangle their competition. Under California’s existing antitrust law, the Cartwright Act, those suits can currently only be taken against multiple businesses acting together.
